title: Renormalized Route Reciprocity and Charged-Fermion Mass Shape in a Chiral SU(15)p Composite Theory
content: This work examines whether the logarithmic shape of the nine charged-fermion masses can be related to reciprocity between composite routes in a confining chiral \(\mathrm{SU}(15)_p\) theory with a Pati--Salam spectator sector. In plain terms, the question is whether two ways of assembling the same composite channel become equivalent after renormalization and thereby account for one specific relation among the observed charged-fermion masses. For \(s\in\{\ell,d,u\}\), define \(A_s=\tfrac14\ln(y_{s,1}y_{s,3}/y_{s,2}^2)\) at a common scale and scheme and \(\Delta_\Pi=A_\ell+2A_d-A_u\). Present inputs place \(\Delta_\Pi=0\) only about \(1.56\sigma\) from the central value, so the relation is treated as a structural hypothesis rather than an empirical law. The fixed route map gives the exact identity \(\Delta_\Pi=C_{21}-C_{12}\). The analysis constructs a positive-metric route involution and proves that invariance of the complete renormalized functional and selected state, together with equivariant renormalization and matching, implies \(C_{12}=C_{21}\); a symmetric vacuum alone is insufficient. For a matched chirality-resolved two-point function, the singular values of \(W_s=F_{L,s}^{-1/2}J_sF_{R,s}^{-1/2}\) determine the charged mass shape without a separate Higgs-vertex reconstruction. It also establishes that charged data leave an exact neutral-sector direction undetermined and therefore do not by themselves predict the neutrino-Dirac curvature. The selected chiral state, determinant modulus (or a demonstrably equivalent Pfaffian formulation), complete source-to-running-mass matching, and controlled continuum limit remain open physical inputs.
